name: Endgame Study

gist.Board of Kings: Area, cheaper for each chess piece he controls. While it is out, a piece cannot be chosen or affected by you as long as a lower-level piece stands in the zone next to it.
gist.Pawn of Kings [W]: One-health pawn, up to eight copies; free to summon with the Board out.
gist.Pawn of Kings [B]: While the Board is out, you cannot remove his Areas.
gist.Kasperov, the King of Kings [B]: Sacrifices a pawn that has survived a turn to put any chess piece from hand or deck in its place.
gist.Knight of Kings [B]: With a Rook and the Board: you cannot move cards out of your deck or discard pile except by drawing.
gist.Bishop of Kings [B]: With a Knight and the Board: the effects of all your heroes are switched off.
gist.Rook of Kings [B]: With a Bishop and the Board: his side ignores anything that would affect more than one of his targets.
gist.Queen of Kings [B]: Counts as Knight, Bishop and Rook at once and stops his other pieces from being switched off.
gist.Queen of Kings [W]: Cheap with pieces out, free to summon, counts as every piece while the Board is out.
gist.Bishop of Kings [W]: Fetches a pawn every turn and puts it straight onto the Board.
gist.Rook of Kings [W]: Turns a pawn sacrifice into another piece from the deck.
gist.Pawn Chain: Reaction: a dead creature is replaced by a pawn from hand or deck.
gist.Pawn Sacrifice: Trades a pawn for three cards.
gist.Castling: Once per game: cancels something aimed at a hero and summons a piece.
gist.Junshi, the Tactical Genius: His Magic Arts spells get cheaper per creature; may act out of turn when a creature dies.

plan: Dom assembles a position. Every chess piece has a single point of health, so the pieces themselves are nothing; the Board of Kings is what matters, because under it a piece cannot be touched while a lower-ranked piece stands beside it. Behind a front of pawns he promotes: the black Knight, Bishop and Rook in the right pairs switch off your hero effects, forbid searching your deck and make his side immune to anything that hits more than one target. Then pawns and Tharx grind you out. Before the Board arrives the whole army dies to a breeze, and afterwards it can still be taken apart from the lowest piece upward, one single-target hit at a time.

looks.early: A scatter of one-health pawns and a Knight; no Board yet.
looks.mid: The Board of Kings laid out, pawns flanking a Bishop and a Rook, your sweepers suddenly doing nothing.
looks.late: Queen, Rook, Bishop and Knight in a line behind pawns; your heroes' effects dark, your deck unsearchable, Dom taking notes.

opening.tell: His pieces all have a single point of health and the Board of Kings is not in play yet.
opening.why: Before the Board every piece dies to any damage at all, and he needs several pieces out to afford the Board; a sweep now sets him back to nothing.

midgame.tell: The Board of Kings is out with white pawns only beside it; no black pawn protects the Area.
midgame.why: The Board is the whole defence: while no black Pawn of Kings is on it, The Yeeting or a free Cataclysm removes it and the one-health army is naked again.

crisis.tell: A black Rook and Bishop stand together, so nothing that hits several targets works; pawns sit at the ends of the row.
crisis.why: Only single-target hits work now, and only on pieces with no lower piece beside them; start with the pawns on the ends and walk up the row, one small hit per piece.

endgame.tell: The position has been broken or traded off and his heroes, never sturdy, are in the open.
endgame.why: The Kasperov deck has no healing and small heroes; once the pieces are few, nothing it has left stops direct damage.
